issues: The alternative sibling-number CXXI and earlier CXVIII are distinct historic methods; their overlap does not create independent experimental replication.
The male/female zodiac-sign attribution to actual brothers and sisters is a historical classification, not scientific sex prediction.
Aspected planets are said to indicate sibling number, but the original does not define the orb/exact eligibility and duplicate counting policies.
Harmful claims of younger-sibling mortality or shortened life are unverified, high-stakes assertions and cannot be applied to actual families.
The third-lord/Sun-Jupiter opposition phrase has ambiguous grammatical antecedents and must not become a deterministic prediction without review.
Birth-order versus best-living-sibling is an explicit either/or alternative, increasing post-hoc opportunities to rescue a failed forecast.
Lilly's purported Ptolemy method is an attribution by Lilly and must be reconciled against original Ptolemy texts separately.
The author's suggestion that Ptolemy's approach may work for siblings from the same mother is a new scope qualification, not a verified observation.
The claim that Ptolemy lacked Greek, Jewish, Arabic and Latin support is a historical authority dispute and not independent validation.
The Latin maxim at the end of the chapter has not been subject to a complete specialist 17th-century diplomatic transcription.
No complete natal datasets, true sibling counts, survival histories, birth-time checks, fertility/infant mortality or prospective control cohorts are provided.
Next original PDF603 starts an unnumbered fourth-house parent/patrimony intro; its clauses belong to a separate archival batch, not CXXI.
